answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 38% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the quartz calculation reruns each epoch, the island weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the velvet settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 185 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 33 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
